hero.title: Fundraising and organisation software for the people who run good causes.
hero.body: Donorfit is a platform for NGOs, nonprofits, charitable trusts, masjids and community organisations. It brings donations, memberships, sponsorships and campaigns into one place, so the people running them spend less time on administration and more time on the work itself.

intro.title: What Donorfit is
intro.lead: Donorfit is a web-based platform that helps organisations collect donations, look after their supporters and run the programmes they raise money for.
intro.p1: Many organisations start with a donation button, a spreadsheet and a lot of goodwill. As they grow, they add a payment provider here, a newsletter tool there, and a folder of receipt templates somewhere else. The work still gets done, but it takes longer than it should, and information ends up spread across tools that don't talk to each other.
intro.p2: Donorfit is built to replace that patchwork with one system. Donation forms, payments through established providers, donor records, receipts and reporting sit together, and specialised modules for memberships, sponsorships, Qurbani, water well projects and group fundraising build on the same foundation. An organisation can start with simple online giving and add more as its needs change.

problem.title: Built around everyday work
problem.p1: Fundraising is rarely only about the donation itself. Someone has to record who gave, send a thank-you and a tax receipt, reconcile payments with the bank, answer questions from supporters and report back on how the money was used. In small teams, that often falls to the same few people, many of them volunteers.
problem.p2: We design Donorfit with those people in mind. Screens are kept clear, routine steps such as receipts are automated where possible, and information entered once is available wherever it's needed. The aim is software that a treasurer, a programme coordinator or a volunteer can pick up without a long training session.

how.title: How organisations use Donorfit
how.integrationsLink: See supported payment and email integrations
how.intro: Every organisation sets things up a little differently, but most use Donorfit for some combination of the following.
how.photo: Volunteers serving food to families at a community charity event

items.title: Collecting donations online and in person
items.text: Customisable donation forms can be embedded on your own website and shared across your channels. QR codes let supporters give from a printed poster or a donation box. Donors can pay with methods such as card, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, SEPA Direct Debit, Bancontact, EPS and iDEAL, processed through supported payment providers.

items.title: Keeping supporter records in one place
items.text: Each contribution is recorded against the donor, so you can see a supporter's history at a glance. Existing records can be imported, and supporters have access to a dedicated donor portal.

items.title: Receipts and thank-yous
items.text: Predefined tax receipt templates let receipts be generated automatically, and system emails can be switched on or off to suit how you work.

items.title: Staying in touch
items.text: Donorfit connects with Brevo and Mailchimp for newsletters, and supports WhatsApp and SMS communication, so updates reach supporters through the channels they already use.

items.title: Working as a team
items.text: Several team members can work in the same account, with reports and dashboards showing how campaigns are doing. For organisations with their own systems, an API and webhooks allow data to flow into other tools.

offer.title: Our products
offer.sub: Alongside general online giving, Donorfit offers modules for specific kinds of programmes. Each one is built for a particular way of raising and managing funds.

products.membership: For associations, clubs and communities with paying members. Manage member records, plans and categories, collect membership fees and keep track of renewals.
products.sponsorship: For organisations that connect sponsors with children, students or projects. Keep track of sponsors, beneficiaries and regular contributions, and share progress with supporters.
products.water-well: For clean water projects. Present each well as a fundraising project, collect contributions towards it and keep supporters informed as the project moves forward.
products.qurbani: For Qurbani campaigns around Eid al-Adha. Let donors choose an animal or share, collect their contributions online and keep a clear record of every order for your team.
products.money-pool: For shared fundraising goals. Several donors contribute towards one target, and everyone can follow the campaign's progress until the goal is reached.
products.school-management: For schools supported by charities and donors. Manage student information, day-to-day administration and fees.

support.title: Who we work with
support.intro: Donorfit is used by organisations of very different sizes and purposes. What they tend to have in common is a small team, a loyal group of supporters and more administration than they would like.
support.photo: An aid worker handing a bottle of cooking oil to a man at a food distribution

items.title: NGOs and nonprofit organisations
items.text: From local initiatives to organisations running projects abroad, NGOs use Donorfit to run appeals, process donations and keep supporter records together instead of across separate tools.

items.title: Charitable trusts and foundations
items.text: Trusts and foundations need a clear record of what came in and where it went. Donorfit keeps contributions, donors and the projects they support connected.

items.title: Masjids and Islamic organisations
items.text: Masjids and Islamic charities often run several kinds of giving at once, from regular community donations to seasonal Qurbani campaigns. Donorfit lets them manage these side by side.

items.title: Educational institutions
items.text: Schools and education charities raise money for buildings, materials and student support. Sponsorship programmes help connect individual students with long-term supporters.

items.title: Community and welfare organisations
items.text: Community groups, associations and welfare organisations use memberships and group fundraising to bring local supporters together around shared goals.

mission.label: Our mission
mission.text: To make fundraising and organisation management simpler, more accessible and more efficient through practical digital solutions.

vision.label: Our vision
vision.text: To help organisations of all sizes use technology to build stronger communities, reach more supporters and achieve more with the resources they have.

values.title: What guides our work
values.intro: These principles shape the decisions we make about the product, from which features we build to how we explain them.
values.photo: Girls in blue headscarves holding up their school textbooks in a classroom

items.title: Simplicity
items.text: Many of the people using Donorfit are volunteers or work part-time. If a task needs a manual to complete, we see that as a problem to solve, not a training issue.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: Supporters want to know where their money goes, and organisations want to know what they are paying for. We try to make both clear, in the product and in how we present it.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text: Useful tools should not be reserved for large organisations with dedicated IT staff. Donorfit is designed so that a small community group can use the same features as a larger charity.

items.title: Reliability
items.text: Organisations depend on their fundraising tools every day, and especially during busy periods such as year-end appeals or Eid. We treat dependable, predictable behaviour as a core requirement.

items.title: Community impact
items.text: We build for organisations whose work improves people's lives. The best measure of our work is how much time and effort it frees up for theirs.

cost.title: How pricing works
cost.p1: The core Donorfit platform is available at €0 per month, with no platform fee and no transaction fee from Donorfit. Donors can choose to cover payment processing fees, so that your organisation receives the full amount of their gift.
cost.p2: Specialised add-ons such as CRM, recurring giving, sponsorship, membership and Qurbani are purchased separately, so you only pay for the modules you use. The platform supports 5 languages and 39 currencies.

items.q: What is Donorfit and how can it benefit us?
items.a: Donorfit is a fundraising platform that helps nonprofits collect donations, manage donors, track interactions and personalise outreach — so you can increase giving and keep supporters engaged for longer.

items.q: How easy is it to set up and use Donorfit?
items.a: Getting started takes three steps: configure your cause settings, connect a payment gateway, and add the donation box to your website.

items.q: What are the payment options available for donation in Donorfit?
items.a: Donorfit supports more than 15 donation payment methods through payment gateways such as Stripe, GoCardless, Mollie and PayPal.

items.q: Can I accept international donations with Donorfit?
items.a: Yes. Through the same payment gateways you can accept contributions in more than 135 currencies.

hero.title: Security, Privacy, and Data Protection at Donorfit
hero.intro: Nonprofits protect vulnerable communities and steward generous public support. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of transparency, data privacy, and technological resilience.

sovereignty.title: European Data Sovereignty
sovereignty.text: All core application infrastructure and relational databases are hosted strictly inside the European Union. We do not transfer non-profit supporter databases or beneficiary dossiers to foreign jurisdictions without explicit adequacy safeguards.

access.title: Strict Access Controls
access.text: We employ strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and mandatory session timeouts. Your organization controls exactly which staff members, volunteers, or auditors can access specific records.

portability.title: Zero Lock-In & Portability
portability.text: You own your organization’s data completely. In accordance with GDPR Article 20, you can export full donor files, giving histories, and active direct debit mandates in standard open formats at any time.

architecture.title: Our Security Architecture & Infrastructure Safeguards
architecture.intro: We practice defense-in-depth across the application lifecycle to defend non-profit operations from unauthorized access, disruption, or data loss.

encryption.title: Encryption in Transit & at Rest
encryption.text: All data transmitted between browsers, mobile devices, and Donorfit servers is protected with Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3). Sensitive databases and backup snapshots are encrypted using AES-256 standard encryption keys.

payments.title: Payment & Banking Rail Security
payments.text: Donations and recurring pledges are processed via PCI-DSS certified European payment facilitators. Bank direct debits follow European EPC SEPA Direct Debit scheme rules with validated IBAN checksums and cryptographically secure mandate IDs.

redundancy.title: Redundancy & Automated Backups
redundancy.text: Application state is continuously backed up with point-in-time recovery capabilities across isolated availability zones in the EU. Disaster recovery plans and data restoration simulations are conducted periodically.

safeguarding.title: Child & Beneficiary Safeguarding
safeguarding.text: For orphan and child sponsorship initiatives, sensitive location metrics and family identities are isolated behind strict role boundaries. Publicly visible profiles require affirmative consent logs and automated identifier redaction.

gdpr.title: GDPR Rights & Data Controller Alignment
gdpr.intro: Under European privacy legislation (EU Regulation 2016/679), your nonprofit acts as the Data Controller, and Donorfit functions as the Data Processor. We provide the technical tooling necessary for you to fulfill all statutory data subject rights.

rights.title: Right to Access (Art. 15)
rights.text: Generate comprehensive donor data dossiers with one click.

rights.title: Right to Erasure (Art. 17)
rights.text: Permanent data deletion tools while respecting statutory tax retention laws.

rights.title: Portability (Art. 20)
rights.text: Export clean, structured CSV and JSON packages without vendor lock-in.

rights.title: Consent Logs (Art. 7)
rights.text: Immutable timestamped records of communication and marketing opt-ins.

items.question: Where is Donorfit platform data physically hosted?
items.answer: All production databases, application servers, and backups are hosted within the European Union (Germany and Ireland) in ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and PCI-DSS compliant data center facilities. We maintain strict EU data sovereignty.

items.question: Does Donorfit store donor credit card numbers or banking passwords?
items.answer: No. Donorfit never stores raw credit card numbers or sensitive payment authentication credentials on our application servers. All payment handling is tokenized through certified Level 1 PCI-DSS payment gateways (such as Stripe and European banking direct debit rails).

items.question: How do you handle Data Processing Agreements (DPA)?
items.answer: Every nonprofit organization using Donorfit enters into a legally binding Data Processing Agreement (DPA) under Article 28 of the GDPR, with standardized technical and organizational measures (TOMs) clearly defined.

items.question: How do you protect sensitive child and beneficiary data in sponsorship programs?
items.answer: Sponsorship modules enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC). Field caseworkers, country directors, and finance teams have distinct permission boundaries. Sensitive records such as medical notes or exact guardian locations can be restricted so only authorized safeguarding officers can view them.

items.question: What is your incident response protocol?
items.answer: In the unlikely event of a security or data breach, our incident response plan requires notification to affected data controllers within 24 to 72 hours in strict alignment with GDPR statutory mandates, alongside immediate containment measures.
